excerpt: Skydive builds AI agents with their own cloud computer that you reach in Slack, email or iMessage. Free pay-as-you-go plan; Starter $20/month.
content:
Skydive lets you build AI agents that do work across your tools. You describe the job, and the agent gets its own computer in the cloud with a browser, terminal and file system, plus its own Slack bot, email inbox and phone number. You can talk to the same agent in Slack, email, iMessage, the web app, the Mac desktop app, a command-line tool or the API, and it keeps one identity and one memory across all of them. Agents connect to apps such as Gmail, GitHub, Notion, Linear, Intercom and Google Drive (the launch post says 900+), and where there is no integration the agent hands you its browser so you can log in.

Agents keep file-based memory in their own git repository, learn from corrections, and can run routines on a schedule or when something happens, so they keep working when your laptop is closed. Several agents can share context and hand work to each other. Credentials are injected through a proxy so the agent does not see raw tokens. Pricing is credit based: model usage is passed through at cost with no markup, and paid plans turn the plan fee into the same amount of usage credit.

Skydive is made by Create, the company behind the AI app builder Anything, and was started by Marcus Lowe and Dhruv Amin. It began as an internal engineering agent nicknamed "Coworker". Skydive launched on Product Hunt on 27 August 2026 and finished #1 for the day and #4 for the week, with 409 upvotes and 105 comments.

We have not tested Skydive ourselves. This page brings together its official site, documentation, pricing and blog, its Product Hunt launch and the official pricing pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.platform: Web, Mac desktop app, Slack, email, iMessage, CLI and API
profile.summary_short: Build AI agent coworkers with their own cloud computer, reachable in Slack, email and iMessage

paragraphs: Marcus Lowe, a co-founder, argues that everyone now has the same AI models but still has to prompt them well. In his view chatbots answer but leave the action to you and forget what you taught them, while workflow builders make you design and maintain every step.

Skydive is meant to sit between the two: you hire an agent for a job, describe it, and it works on its own cloud computer and codebase, picks up your skills or writing style when asked, and improves by learning from earlier conversations.
launch_story.attribution: Marcus Lowe, maker, on Product Hunt

use_cases: An executive-assistant agent that handles your inbox and scheduling
A support agent that answers in Intercom or Slack
An engineering agent that debugs and opens pull requests
A marketing agent that makes ad creative and checks campaigns
Routines such as a morning digest or a weekly report

fit: want agents that act in your tools rather than only chat
work across Slack, email and phone and want one agent that remembers everything
prefer to describe the outcome instead of building workflows step by step
not_fit: need fixed, predictable automations: a workflow tool such as n8n may suit better
need a fixed monthly bill: usage draws down a credit balance and can need top-ups
need SSO, SAML or audit logs on a small budget: these are Enterprise-only

pricing.intro: Skydive is subscription based. Paid plans include usage credit equal to the plan fee, and model usage is charged at cost with no markup. Prices are flat per workspace, not per seat.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: Starts with a small amount of credit, no card required; buy credit as you go; community support

plans.name: Starter
plans.detail: $20 of usage credit a month, unlimited agents and seats, email support. Yearly: $240 with $264 of credit

plans.name: Team
plans.detail: $200 of usage credit a month, unlimited agents and seats, priority support. Yearly: $2,400 with $2,640 of credit

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: SSO and SAML, audit logs, advanced security, custom contracts, dedicated support

notes: Credit is spent on model usage (at cost), sandbox compute and metered services such as search and email. Extra credit starts at $50, and auto-refill and monthly spend caps are available.
If a workspace runs out of credit, agents drop to a limited free floor until more credit is added.

alternatives.intro: Like-for-like AI agent and automation tools, picked by us. Prices come from each product's own pricing page, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: Lindy
items.what: No-code AI agents and assistants for email, meetings and business tasks
items.starts_at: Free $50 of credits for 7 days; Team from $29.99 a month
items.difference: Bills each active user and pools credits, while Skydive charges a flat workspace fee with model usage at cost.

items.name: Relevance AI
items.what: Platform for building an 'AI workforce' of agents for sales and operations
items.difference: Aimed at company-wide deployments sold through sales, while Skydive has self-serve plans from free.

items.name: n8n
items.what: Workflow automation with AI steps, cloud or self-hosted
items.starts_at: Starter €20 a month billed annually; self-hosted version on GitHub
items.difference: You design each workflow step yourself, the approach Skydive's makers contrast their product with.

liked: Focusing on the outcome rather than writing prompts
asked: Whether it is chat-only (makers: there is a full web app, plus Slack, email, iMessage, desktop, CLI and API)
Whether access can be limited per agent (makers: each agent gets only the integrations it is given, and can be private, internal or external)
How it decides when to ask a human (makers: you set what each agent owns and what needs approval)
What it actually does, from a commenter who found the launch unclear

pros: One agent with shared memory across Slack, email, iMessage, web, desktop and terminal
Each agent has its own cloud computer, so it can browse, run code and host apps
Model usage billed at cost with no markup, and a free pay-as-you-go start
Per-agent access scoping and visibility settings; makers say it is SOC 2 compliant
cons: Costs depend on usage, so the monthly bill can vary
SSO, SAML and audit logs only on Enterprise
Many launch-day comments came from the team itself or were flagged by Product Hunt as likely AI-written, so independent feedback is thin
Agent memory is shared with everyone who talks to the agent, so it is not a place for secrets (its FAQ says so)

faq.a: A tool for building AI agents that each have their own cloud computer, memory and identity. You reach them in Slack, email, iMessage, the web app, the Mac app, the CLI or the API, and they do multi-step work in your connected tools.
Free is $0 a month, pay as you go. Starter is $20 a month and Team is $200 a month, each including the same amount in usage credit. Enterprise is custom. Model usage is charged at cost.
No. Its FAQ says most people build and run agents through conversation; the agents write and run code in their own sandbox.

faq.q: Can I limit what an agent can access?
faq.a: Yes. Each agent only gets the integrations you give it, and it can be private, internal to your workspace or external. Credentials are injected through a proxy so the agent does not see raw tokens.

faq.q: Does it work when my computer is off?
faq.a: Yes. Agents run in the cloud and can follow routines on a schedule or when an event happens.
Create, the company behind the AI app builder Anything, founded by Marcus Lowe and Dhruv Amin, according to Skydive's blog.
Lindy for no-code AI assistants, Relevance AI for enterprise agent teams, and n8n if you prefer to build workflows step by step.
